Causal-forest (`grf::causal_forest`) estimates of treatment-effect heterogeneity, with SHAP variable importance
(`fastshap`, `nsim = 50`), for 8 outcome x study x treatment-arm combinations. The forests are slow
(`num.trees = 2000`), so the analysis can be knit on its own.

For each combination the script runs `grf::test_calibration()` (an omnibus test of whether the forest detected any
treatment-effect heterogeneity) and `grf::best_linear_projection()` (per-covariate tests). The beeswarm plots show every
predictor ranked by SHAP importance; covariates with BLP `p < .05` are starred on their label, because SHAP importance is
not itself a significance test. The text above each plot reports the omnibus calibration p-value and the number of
starred covariates. With this many simultaneous tests, a few starred covariates are expected by chance, so they should not
be reported as findings without a multiplicity correction. The final section ("Headline Figure") re-fits SHAP at
`max_display = 12` for the two Belief-Tailored-vs.-control contrasts on the primary outcome and saves `figures/supplement/fig-causal-forest.png`.
`09b_heterogeneity_checks.R` adds further diagnostics and writes the table used in the supplement.

# Causal Forests

```{r causal forest, eval=TRUE, results='asis'}

# Trimmed to the two headline DVs (2020 Denialism, Claim Certainty).
# Restore to `dvs_post` for all 8 outcomes.
cf_outcomes <- c("ER0Norm_Post", "Sureness_Post_1")
cf_tune <- FALSE
cf_num_trees <- 2000

cf_predictors_base <- c(
  "ER0Norm_Pre_center", "ERNorm_Pre_center", "ER1_Pre_center", "ER2_Pre_center",
  "Sureness_Pre_center", "AffPol_Pre", "Race", "Age", "GenderClean", "Education",
  "religion", "DemRep_C.text", "EconomicConservatism", "SocialConservatism",
  "VoteMethod.text", "PartyAffil.text", "PartyReg.text", "VoteFor2020.clean",
  "Vote_1", "InstTrust_USGov", "InstTrust_CivilService",
  "InstTrust_Media", "InstTrust_Banks", "InstTrust_MajorCompanies",
  "genai_trust", "genai_fam_1", "genai_use_1"
)

# Study 1 has interface variation (Qualtrics vs. Chat); Study 2 does not.
cf_predictors_s1 <- c("ConditionChat", cf_predictors_base)
cf_predictors_s2 <- cf_predictors_base

# Study 1's control is Adversarial Dialogue (no Control rows exist there).
# Study 2's control is Control (cats & dogs), with Adversarial Dialogue as a second treatment arm.
# Each study is run separately so no comparison crosses studies without shared
# randomization behind it.
cf_control_level_s1 <- "Adversarial Dialogue"
cf_treatment_levels_s1 <- c("Belief-Tailored", "Belief & Values-Tailored")

cf_control_level_s2 <- "Control"
cf_treatment_levels_s2 <- c("Belief-Tailored", "Adversarial Dialogue")

cf_label_map <- rf_label_map

clean_mm_var <- function(var_name, label_map) {
  label_map_clean <- setNames(unname(label_map), gsub("\\.", "_", names(label_map)))
  name <- gsub("\\.", "_", var_name)
  matches <- names(label_map_clean)[vapply(names(label_map_clean), function(b) startsWith(name, b), logical(1))]

  if (length(matches) > 0) {
    base <- matches[which.max(nchar(matches))]
    level <- substring(name, nchar(base) + 1)
    level <- gsub("^_", "", level)
    level <- gsub("_", " ", level)
    if (nzchar(level)) {
      return(paste0(label_map_clean[[base]], ": ", level))
    }
    return(label_map_clean[[base]])
  }

  name <- gsub("_", " ", name)
  name <- gsub("(?<=[a-z])(?=[A-Z])", " ", name, perl = TRUE)
  name
}

coerce_labelled <- function(x) {
  if (!any(grepl("labelled", class(x)))) {
    return(x)
  }
  labs <- labelled::val_labels(x)
  if (length(labs) == 0) {
    # A factor's levels are its labels -- as.numeric() on a factor returns raw
    # integer codes, not category names, so preserve factors (and characters)
    # via as.character() rather than falling through to as.numeric().
    if (is.character(x) || is.factor(x)) {
      return(as.character(x))
    }
    return(as.numeric(x))
  }
  labelled::to_factor(x, levels = "labels")
}

# Colors are per-DV so plots for the two outcomes are visually distinguishable
# at a glance: navy (the paper's primary color) for the main DV, teal (the
# paper's existing secondary color, colpal.2 in the parent script) for the
# secondary one. Falls back to navy for any outcome not listed.
cf_dv_colors <- list(
  ER0Norm_Post    = list(low = "#AEB9E0", high = "#0B1B66"),
  Sureness_Post_1 = list(low = "#B7E4DF", high = "#20A49C")
)

sig_stars <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "",
    p < .001 ~ "***",
    p < .01  ~ "**",
    p < .05  ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ ""
  )
}

run_cf_shap <- function(data, outcome, treat_level, control_level, predictors, label_map, min_n = 50, max_display = Inf) {
  cf_data <- data %>%
    filter(ConditionFeedback %in% c(treat_level, control_level)) %>%
    select(all_of(c(outcome, "ConditionFeedback", predictors))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome]]))

  y_vec <- cf_data[[outcome]]
  if (any(grepl("labelled", class(y_vec)))) {
    y_vec <- labelled::unlabelled(y_vec, user_na_to_na = TRUE)
  }
  if (is.factor(y_vec)) {
    y_vec <- as.numeric(as.character(y_vec))
  } else {
    y_vec <- as.numeric(y_vec)
  }

  x_df <- cf_data %>%
    select(-all_of(outcome)) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), coerce_labelled)) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.character), ~tidyr::replace_na(.x, "Missing"))) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), ~forcats::fct_na_value_to_level(.x, level = "Missing")))

  keep <- !is.na(y_vec) & is.finite(y_vec)
  if (!all(keep)) {
    y_vec <- y_vec[keep]
    x_df <- x_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  num_cols <- names(x_df)[vapply(x_df, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  for (col in num_cols) {
    if (all(is.na(x_df[[col]]))) {
      next
    }
    med <- median(x_df[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
    x_df[[col]][is.na(x_df[[col]])] <- med
  }

  if (nrow(x_df) < min_n || length(unique(x_df$ConditionFeedback)) < 2) {
    message("Skipping ", outcome, " (", treat_level, " vs ", control_level, "): insufficient data")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # model.matrix(~0+.) needs every factor to have >=2 observed levels in this
  # specific filtered subset, or its contrasts break -- which column degenerates
  # can differ across the 8 outcome x study x treatment combinations this loop runs.
  predictor_cols <- setdiff(names(x_df), "ConditionFeedback")
  constant_cols <- predictor_cols[vapply(predictor_cols, function(col) {
    length(unique(stats::na.omit(x_df[[col]]))) < 2
  }, logical(1))]
  if (length(constant_cols) > 0) {
    message("Dropping constant predictor(s) for ", outcome, " (", treat_level, " vs ", control_level, "): ",
            paste(constant_cols, collapse = ", "))
    x_df <- x_df %>% select(-all_of(constant_cols))
  }

  W <- as.integer(x_df$ConditionFeedback == treat_level)

  fit_result <- tryCatch({
    X <- model.matrix(~ 0 + ., data = x_df %>% select(-ConditionFeedback))
    X <- as.matrix(X)
    storage.mode(X) <- "double"
    Y <- y_vec

    cf_model <- grf::causal_forest(
      X, Y, W,
      tune.parameters = if (cf_tune) "all" else "none",
      num.trees = cf_num_trees,
      seed = 1234
    )
    list(X = X, Y = Y, cf_model = cf_model)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("FAILED for ", outcome, " (", treat_level, " vs ", control_level, "): ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })

  if (is.null(fit_result)) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  X <- fit_result$X
  Y <- fit_result$Y
  cf_model <- fit_result$cf_model

  # Omnibus test: is there any real treatment-effect heterogeneity here at
  # all? (differential.forest.prediction significant = yes.) This doesn't
  # identify which covariate drives it -- that's what BLP is for below -- but
  # it's the honest check on whether the beeswarm's spread is signal or noise.
  cal <- tryCatch(grf::test_calibration(cf_model), error = function(e) e)
  cal_p <- if (inherits(cal, "error")) NA_real_ else cal["differential.forest.prediction", "Pr(>t)"]

  # Per-covariate significance via best_linear_projection(), grf's own
  # recommended inferential tool for "which covariates predict the treatment
  # effect" (unlike SHAP importance, which has no null distribution attached).
  # This is ANNOTATION, not a filter: every predictor still gets plotted below
  # (full descriptive picture, same as before), significant ones just get
  # stars on their label. An earlier version hard-filtered to p<.05 only --
  # but with every one of the 8 combos failing the omnibus calibration test,
  # that left 5/8 plots empty and the other 3 showing 1-3 rows out of 38-52,
  # which threw out the exploratory value the full picture had.
  #
  # Two gotchas in mapping p-values back to X's columns, both found by
  # actually running this on the real 52-column S1 predictor set before
  # trusting it:
  # 1. best_linear_projection() builds a data.frame(A) internally, which
  #    applies make.names(unique=TRUE) to column names -- silently turning
  #    spaces into periods (e.g. "DemRep_C.textLean Republican" becomes
  #    "DemRep_C.textLean.Republican" in blp's rownames). String-matching
  #    raw colnames(X) against that would miss every multi-word dummy column.
  # 2. It can also silently DROP columns that are collinear/aliased in this
  #    specific filtered subset (52 in, 43 rows out was observed) -- so row
  #    count isn't guaranteed to match ncol(X) either; those columns just get
  #    no star (NA p-value), same treatment as a non-significant one.
  # Fix: build a mangled-name -> original-name lookup with the same
  # make.names() call blp uses internally, then look up only the rownames
  # blp actually returned.
  blp <- tryCatch(grf::best_linear_projection(cf_model, A = X), error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(blp, "error")) {
    message("best_linear_projection() failed for ", outcome, " (", treat_level, " vs ", control_level, "): ", conditionMessage(blp))
    pvals <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, ncol(X)), colnames(X))
  } else {
    name_lookup <- setNames(colnames(X), make.names(colnames(X), unique = TRUE))
    blp_rows <- setdiff(rownames(blp), "(Intercept)")
    pvals <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, ncol(X)), colnames(X))
    pvals[name_lookup[blp_rows]] <- blp[blp_rows, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  }
  n_sig <- sum(!is.na(pvals) & pvals < .05)

  pred_wrapper <- function(object, newdata) {
    predict(object, as.matrix(newdata))$predictions
  }

  set.seed(1234)
  shap_vals <- fastshap::explain(
    cf_model,
    X = as.data.frame(X),
    pred_wrapper = pred_wrapper,
    nsim = 50,
    adjust = TRUE
  )

  # Drop any feature that's NA on every SHAP simulation (fastshap can produce
  # these for degenerate dummy columns) before handing off to shapviz, which
  # otherwise errors on all-NA columns.
  keep_feat <- !apply(shap_vals, 2, function(col) all(is.na(col)))
  shap_vals <- shap_vals[, keep_feat, drop = FALSE]
  X <- X[, keep_feat, drop = FALSE]

  # Clean + wrap variable names, append significance stars from BLP (blank for
  # non-significant/untested columns), applied identically to shap_vals and X
  # so shapviz can match them by name.
  raw_cols <- colnames(shap_vals)
  clean_names <- vapply(raw_cols, clean_mm_var, character(1), label_map = label_map)
  clean_names <- stringr::str_wrap(clean_names, width = 40)
  clean_names <- paste0(clean_names, " ", vapply(pvals[raw_cols], sig_stars, character(1)))
  colnames(shap_vals) <- clean_names
  X_named <- as.data.frame(X)
  colnames(X_named) <- clean_names

  outcome_label <- dplyr::recode(outcome, !!!new_labels, .default = outcome)
  col_pair <- cf_dv_colors[[outcome]]
  if (is.null(col_pair)) col_pair <- list(low = "#AEB9E0", high = "#0B1B66")

  title_text <- stringr::str_wrap(
    paste0("SHAP: ", outcome_label, " (", treat_level, " vs ", control_level, ")"),
    width = 55
  )

  sv <- shapviz::shapviz(shap_vals, X = X_named)
  p <- shapviz::sv_importance(sv, kind = "beeswarm", max_display = max_display) +
    scale_color_gradient(low = col_pair$low, high = col_pair$high, name = "Feature value") +
    labs(title = title_text) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(size = 12),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 15, r = 15, b = 10, l = 10)
    )

  list(plot = p, n_features = ncol(shap_vals), n_sig = n_sig, n_tested = ncol(X), cal_p = cal_p)
}

cf_base_s1 <- df_both %>% filter(Study == 1)
cf_base_s2 <- df_both %>% filter(Study == 2)

cf_shap_results <- list()

# fig.width/fig.height set per-plot via knitr::opts_current$set() just before
# each print() -- the 8 combos have different feature counts (constant
# predictors get dropped per-subset), so a single fixed chunk-level size
# either crops the biggest plots or wastes space on the smaller ones.
emit_cf_plot <- function(res, study_label, outcome_label, treat_level, control_level, key) {
  if (is.null(res)) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat("\n\n#### ", study_label, ": ", outcome_label, " -- ", treat_level, " vs. ", control_level, "\n\n", sep = "")
  cal_txt <- if (is.na(res$cal_p)) "calibration test failed" else paste0("omnibus heterogeneity test (differential.forest.prediction) p = ", format.pval(res$cal_p, digits = 3))
  cat("*", cal_txt, "; ", res$n_sig, " of ", res$n_tested, " covariates significant in the best linear projection (p < .05, starred on the plot below).*\n\n", sep = "")

  cf_shap_results[[key]] <<- res$plot
  knitr::opts_current$set(fig.width = 11, fig.height = max(6, res$n_features * 0.26 + 2))
  print(res$plot)
  cat("\n\n---\n\n")
}

for (outcome in cf_outcomes) {
  outcome_label <- dplyr::recode(outcome, !!!new_labels, .default = outcome)
  for (treat_level in cf_treatment_levels_s1) {
    res <- run_cf_shap(cf_base_s1, outcome, treat_level, cf_control_level_s1, cf_predictors_s1, cf_label_map)
    emit_cf_plot(res, "Study 1", outcome_label, treat_level, cf_control_level_s1, paste("S1", outcome, treat_level, sep = "_"))
  }
  for (treat_level in cf_treatment_levels_s2) {
    res <- run_cf_shap(cf_base_s2, outcome, treat_level, cf_control_level_s2, cf_predictors_s2, cf_label_map)
    emit_cf_plot(res, "Study 2", outcome_label, treat_level, cf_control_level_s2, paste("S2", outcome, treat_level, sep = "_"))
  }
}

# cf_shap_results is keyed "S{study}_{outcome}_{treatment}", e.g.
# cf_shap_results[["S1_ER0Norm_Post_Belief-Tailored"]]. The full all-covariate
# beeswarms above (max_display = Inf, 38-52 predictors each) are the
# Supplement's exhaustive record of all 8 outcome x study x arm combinations.

```

# Headline Figure: 2020 Denialism, Belief-Tailored vs. Study Control

```{r headline figure, eval=TRUE}

# A single readable figure rather than all 38-52 covariates: re-fit SHAP at max_display = 12 (top predictors by
# mean |SHAP|) for the two flagship Belief-Tailored-vs.-control contrasts on the primary outcome. The full 52/38-covariate
# versions of the same two comparisons are in cf_shap_results (S1_ER0Norm_Post_Belief-Tailored,
# S2_ER0Norm_Post_Belief-Tailored).

headline_s1 <- run_cf_shap(cf_base_s1, "ER0Norm_Post", "Belief-Tailored",
                            cf_control_level_s1, cf_predictors_s1, cf_label_map,
                            max_display = 12)
headline_s2 <- run_cf_shap(cf_base_s2, "ER0Norm_Post", "Belief-Tailored",
                            cf_control_level_s2, cf_predictors_s2, cf_label_map,
                            max_display = 12)

cat("Study 1 (Belief-Tailored vs. Adversarial Dialogue): omnibus p = ",
    format.pval(headline_s1$cal_p, digits = 3), ", ", headline_s1$n_sig,
    "/", headline_s1$n_tested, " covariates BLP-significant\n", sep = "")
cat("Study 2 (Belief-Tailored vs. Cats & Dogs Control): omnibus p = ",
    format.pval(headline_s2$cal_p, digits = 3), ", ", headline_s2$n_sig,
    "/", headline_s2$n_tested, " covariates BLP-significant\n", sep = "")

fig_causal_forest <- (
  headline_s1$plot + labs(title = NULL, subtitle = "Study 1: Belief-Tailored vs. Adversarial Dialogue")
) + (
  headline_s2$plot + labs(title = NULL, subtitle = "Study 2: Belief-Tailored vs. Cats & Dogs Control")
) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "SHAP Variable Importance: Heterogeneity in Treatment Effects on 2020 Denialism",
    tag_levels = "A"
  )

print(fig_causal_forest)

ggsave("figures/supplement/fig-causal-forest.png", fig_causal_forest, width = 14, height = 7, dpi = 300, create.dir = TRUE)

```
